passages.text: AIR, a thin, invisible, elastic fluid, which surrounds the earth to a considerable height, and is necessary to the life of animals and to the burning of fire.

It was long reckoned one of the four elements; but the modern chemists have shown it to be a compound of two kinds of air: vital or dephlogisticated air, which supports flame and life, and azote, or phlogisticated air, in which an animal dies.
Of these the vital air makes about one part in four, and the azote nearly three parts.
The air has weight, as Torricelli proved; its pressure supports a column of mercury of about thirty inches in the barometer.
It grows thinner as we ascend, and is supposed not to extend above forty-five miles from the earth.
Fixed air, which is found in small quantity in the atmosphere, is produced by breathing and by burning, and is fatal to animals.
The atmosphere of Earth is the layer of gases, known together as air, held by Earth's gravity. It protects life and makes breathing possible.
Dry air contains about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen, with small amounts of argon, carbon dioxide and other gases.
Oxygen was isolated in the 1770s by Carl Wilhelm Scheele and Joseph Priestley and named by Antoine Lavoisier, who showed that air is a mixture of gases and not an element.
Air pressure at sea level is about 101 kilopascals, equal to a column of mercury about 760 millimetres high. Evangelista Torricelli invented the mercury barometer in 1643.
Air becomes thinner with height. There is no definite upper boundary; the Karman line at 100 kilometres is often used as the edge of space.
Carbon dioxide makes up about 0.04% of the air. It is released by respiration and by burning fuels, and it traps heat in the atmosphere.

reasons: The 1797 entry describes the air around the earth, which Wikipedia covers under Atmosphere of Earth.
Rare terms appear in both: Torricelli, barometer, column of mercury, proportions of the two main gases.
Air (classical element) scores on the headword but covers only the old idea of four elements.

alignments.label: Not an element

britannica.quote: It was long reckoned one of the four elements; but the modern chemists have shown it to be a compound

wikipedia.quote: air is a mixture of gases and not an element

alignments.note: Right that air is not an element. It is a mixture, not a compound: its gases are not chemically joined.

alignments.label: Vital air

britannica.quote: vital or dephlogisticated air, which supports flame and life

alignments.note: A change in language: vital or dephlogisticated air is oxygen.

alignments.label: Azote

britannica.quote: azote, or phlogisticated air, in which an animal dies

alignments.note: Azote is nitrogen. The French still call it azote.

alignments.label: The proportions

britannica.quote: the vital air makes about one part in four

alignments.note: Close: one in four is 25%, today's figure is 21%.

alignments.label: Weight of the air

britannica.quote: supports a column of mercury of about thirty inches

wikipedia.quote: a column of mercury about 760 millimetres high

alignments.note: 760 millimetres is just under thirty inches.

alignments.label: Height of the air

britannica.quote: is supposed not to extend above forty-five miles

wikipedia.quote: There is no definite upper boundary

alignments.note: Thinner with height is right. A fixed edge at 45 miles is not.

alignments.label: Fixed air

britannica.quote: produced by breathing and by burning

wikipedia.quote: released by respiration and by burning fuels

alignments.note: Fixed air is carbon dioxide; its sources are the same.

alignments.label: Greenhouse gas

wikipedia.quote: it traps heat in the atmosphere

alignments.note: The 1797 entry sees fixed air only as a poison to animals.

suggestedQuestions: What are vital air and azote called today?
Was the 1797 entry right about what air is made of?

What are vital air and azote called toda.answer: Vital air, which supports flame and life, is oxygen; azote, in which an animal dies, is nitrogen [B2]. Wikipedia names the same two gases as oxygen and nitrogen [W2] [W3].

Was the 1797 entry right about what air.answer: Mostly. It says air is not an element but made of vital air, about one part in four, and azote, nearly three parts [B2] [B3]. Wikipedia gives 21% oxygen and 78% nitrogen [W2], and calls air a mixture rather than a compound [W3].
